newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs rocket on "tankan", CDs, insurers' bond plan.
newsitem.headline: JGBs rocket on "tankan", CDs, insurers' bond plan.

text.p: Cash Japanese government bonds (JGBs) and futures rocketed on a variety of bullish factors on Wednesday, such as only a slight recovery in business sentiment as seen in the Bank of Japan's key quarterly "tankan" corporate survey and falls in key money market rates, traders said.
The key December JGB futures contract rose to a high of 126.30 in late afternoon compared with Tuesday's 125.30. It closed the session with handsome gains at 126.04.
The rate on key three-month certificates of deposit fell to a 11-month low of 0.50 percent after the "tankan".

The tankan's headline diffusion index (DI) of major manufacturers' business sentiment improved to minus three in November from minus seven in August. But the widely watched DI forecast for March 1997 stayed in negative territory at minus one, showing only a slight improvement in corporate sentiment.
"The tankan only re-confirmed the market belief the BOJ is never going to move until it examines the deflationary impact of a planned tax hike in April," said a city bank trader.
Traders said weak corporate sentiment for March, combined with the tax hike, could slow economic recovery further in 1997.

Masayuki Matsushima, director of the BOJ's research and statistics department, said on Wednesday that companies are cautious about their outlook and that companies of all sizes have revised down their profit outlook for the latter half of this fiscal year, which ends next March.
The benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB yield fell to 2.470 percent, plunging from 2.565 percent Tuesday. Large-lot buying in the 190th JGB was detected in the morning, traders said.
Meanwhile, the bonds' bull run was spurred further in the afternoon by life insurers' announcement of portfolio plans for the latter half of 1996/97.
Sumitomo Life Insurance said it plans 400 to 500 billion yen worth of new investment in domestic bonds in the second half of 1996/97.
Meiji Life said it plans 70 billion yen worth of fresh investment in the domestic bonds in the same period.
Foreign accounts, though quiet compared with local city banks, were making fresh long positions in the next benchmark March contract.
The market is waiting for Japan's industrial production due out Thursday, which was widely expected to show healthy growth. -- Yoshiko Mori, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8676
